section_entries.label: 1. Introduction
section_entries.mathematical_role: Defines continuous and zero-sampled moments, recalls the arithmetic/random-matrix factorization, and motivates an offset family intended to interpolate between value and derivative statistics.

neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The characteristic polynomial of a Haar unitary matrix is matched to zeta at height T by setting matrix dimension to the local logarithmic density, and its Barnes-G asymptotic supplies the previously unknown universal coefficient.

section_entries.label: 3. Conjecture and limiting consequences
section_entries.mathematical_role: Transfers the random-matrix offset profile to zeros of zeta and derives the derivative and macroscopically shifted moment regimes from its small- and large-offset limits.

unit_result_entry.title: Shifted discrete zeta moments inherit the random-matrix crossover profile
unit_result_entry.why_material: Conjecture 5 transfers F_k to values of zeta displaced from its zeros by alpha local spacings, preserving the arithmetic factor and Barnes-G factor and demanding uniformity over a growing alpha range.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: This is a number-theoretic conjecture under the paper's standing setup, not a consequence of the random-matrix theorem.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Wilf-Zeilberger telescoping collapses the double series to the profile series
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Coefficient comparison reduces equality of the double and single profile series to a finite identity; a generated WZ pair makes the difference telescope, proves independence from the coefficient index, and fixes the constant at the base case.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: The zero-offset limit recovers derivative moments
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Dividing the shifted value by the offset and using the small-alpha leading term of F_k converts Conjecture 5 into the derivative-moment conjecture with the correct Barnes-G shift and logarithmic exponent.

section_entries.label: 3.1. Number-theoretic comparisons
section_entries.mathematical_role: Compares the offset conjecture with a proved k=1 formula and a k=2 mollified theorem whose forbidden endpoint extrapolation reproduces the predicted profile and derivative moment.

unit_result_entry.title: The extrapolated k=2 profile reproduces the fourth derivative moment constant
unit_result_entry.why_material: Applying the same small-offset argument to the conditional k=2 profile yields the eighth-logarithmic-scale fourth moment of zeta prime and agrees with the earlier derivative conjecture.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: This inherits both the impermissible eta=1 extrapolation and the offset-limit reasoning; it is not an unconditional theorem.
unit_dependency_entry.representation_dependency: The numerical constant and power are formula-sensitive and should be checked against the PDF.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: A mollified k=2 theorem matches the profile only after an unproved endpoint extrapolation
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The available number-theoretic theorem controls a zeta value multiplied by a short Dirichlet polynomial for eta below one half; formally setting eta=1 turns the polynomial into zeta and the resulting series simplifies exactly to the predicted F_2 profile.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: The profile has a theorem-level comparison at k=1, whereas the k=2 agreement and derivative constant require pushing a mollifier-length parameter outside the proved range.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The conditional k=2 match must not be reported as equivalent in evidential status to the RH-conditional k=1 theorem.
